     8	/-!
     9	# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract
    10	
    11	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
    12	This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
    13	always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
    14	`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
    15	arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
    16	explicit obligations.
    17	
    18	The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
    19	second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
    21	through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    38	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    42	
    43	/-! ## The native adapter contract -/
    44	
    45	/--
    46	A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
    47	cocycle datum.
    48	
    49	The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
    50	certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
    51	calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
    52	evaluation module.
    53	-/
    54	structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    55	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    57	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    58	  represents :
    59	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    60	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    61	  datum_class :
    62	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    63	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    64	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    65	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    66	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    67	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    68	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    69	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    70	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
    71	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    72	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    73	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    74	  h0_rank_one :
    75	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    76	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    77	
    78	namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation
    79	
    80	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    81	
    82	/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.
    83	
    84	The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
    85	without weakening or adding hypotheses.
    86	-/
    87	noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    88	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    89	    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
    90	  { cover := P.cover
    91	    representative := P.representative
    92	    represents := P.represents
    93	    datum := P.datum
    94	    datum_class := P.datum_class
    95	    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    96	    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    97	    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    98	    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    99	    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
   100	    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
   101	    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
   102	    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }
   103	
   104	theorem nonempty_localPresentation
   105	    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
   106	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
   107	  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩
   108	
   109	end PicRankOneNativePresentation
   110	
   111	/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/
   112	
   113	/--
   114	An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
   115	consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
   116	`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
   117	choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
   118	-/
   119	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
   120	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   121	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   122	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   123	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
   124	        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
   125	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
   126	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   127	  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
   128	  intro A _ _ t
   129	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
   130	  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation
   131	
   132	end AlgebraicGeometry

     7	/-!
     8	# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum
     9	
    10	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
    11	ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
    12	modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
    13	that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
    14	`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
    15	`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
    16	restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.
    17	
    18	The canonical piece trivializations also prove that the native module is a line
    19	bundle.  Pushforward base-change and existence of a tied
    20	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` remain genuine producer obligations.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    32	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    34	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    35	
    36	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    41	
    42	/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.
    43	
    44	The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
    45	are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
    46	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    47	    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    48	      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
    49	  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    50	    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
    51	  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    52	      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    53	    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
    54	  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    55	    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    56	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    57	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    58	    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)
    59	
    60	/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
    61	noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
    62	  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    63	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
    64	  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    65	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    66	    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
    67	  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    68	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
    69	  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    70	    intro X Y f r m
    71	    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
    72	        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
    73	      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
    74	        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
    75	        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    76	    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    77	    apply Subtype.ext
    78	    funext j
    79	    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    80	    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])
    81	
    82	/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
    83	noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
    84	  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
    85	  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    86	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
    87	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    88	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    89	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    90	    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
    91	  all_goals rfl

    93	/-! ## Piecewise line-bundle trivializations -/
    94	
    95	/-- Sections of the native module over one cocycle piece are the structure-ring sections.
    96	
    97	The open-immersion ring equivalence transports the component trivialization from the ambient
    98	relative curve to the restricted scheme.  The `gluedTriv_gluedQsmul` identity is exactly the
    99	structure-sheaf semilinearity needed for this to be a linear equivalence over the restricted
   100	ring of sections. -/
   101	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv
   102	    (j : D.index) (V : (D.pieces j).toScheme.Opens) :
   103	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) ≃ₗ[
   104	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) := by
   105	  let e := gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   106	  let ρ := ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   107	  let f : Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) →ₗ[
   108	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) :=
   109	    { toFun := fun s => ρ (e s)
   110	      map_add' := by
   111	        intro s t
   112	        change ρ (e (s + t)) = ρ (e s) + ρ (e t)
   113	        change ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t)) =
   114	          ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s) +
   115	            ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t)
   116	        rw [show gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t) =
   117	            gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s +
   118	              gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t by
   119	              exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).map_add s t]
   120	        exact ρ.map_add _ _
   121	      map_smul' := by
   122	        intro r s
   123	        change ρ
   124	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   125	              (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl) (ρ.symm r) s)) =
   126	          r * ρ
   127	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s)
   128	        rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul]
   129	        simp [ρ] }
   130	  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective f
   131	  constructor
   132	  · intro s t h
   133	    have h' := congrArg ρ.symm h
   134	    dsimp [f] at h'
   135	    rw [ρ.symm_apply_apply, ρ.symm_apply_apply] at h'
   136	    exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).injective h'
   137	  · intro r
   138	    refine ⟨e.symm (ρ.symm r), ?_⟩
   139	    change ρ (e (e.symm (ρ.symm r))) = r
   140	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, ρ.apply_symm_apply]
   141	
   142	/-- The piecewise section equivalences assemble to a sheaf isomorphism with the unit module. -/
   143	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSheafIso (j : D.index) :
   144	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D) ≅
   145	      SheafOfModules.unit (D.pieces j).toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   146	  (SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _).preimageIso
   147	    (PresheafOfModules.isoMk
   148	      (fun V => (nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv D j V.unop).toModuleIso)
   149	      (fun {V W} f => by
   150	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   151	        apply LinearMap.ext
   152	        intro x
   153	        change
   154	          ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso W.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   155	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le W.unop)
   156	                (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
   157	                  ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop)) x)) =
   158	            (D.pieces j).toScheme.presheaf.map f
   159	              (((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   160	                (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x))
   161	        rw [gluedTriv_res B D.isGluingCocycle j
   162	          ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   163	          ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x]
   164	        simp only [Scheme.Opens.ι_appIso]
   165	        change
   166	          (relCurve C B).resHom
   167	              ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   168	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   169	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x) =
   170	            (relCurve C B).presheaf.map
   171	              ((D.pieces j).ι.opensFunctor.map f.unop).op
   172	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   173	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x)
   174	        rfl))
   175	
   176	/-- The canonical native module is locally a free rank-one structure-sheaf module. -/
   177	theorem nativeModule_isLineBundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle (nativeModule D) := by
   178	  intro x
   179	  let j := D.pieceIndex x
   180	  refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
   181	  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩
   182	
   183	/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
   184	the datum's original module of sections.
   185	
   186	The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
   187	point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
   188	of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
   189	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
   190	    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
   191	    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   192	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
   193	      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
   194	  let f :
   195	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   196	        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
   197	        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
   198	    { toFun := fun x => x
   199	      map_add' := by
   200	        intros
   201	        rfl
   202	      map_smul' := by
   203	        intro r x
   204	        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
   205	            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
   206	          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
   207	        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
   208	          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
   209	  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩
   210	
   211	/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.
   212	
   213	This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
   214	presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
   215	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
   216	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   217	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
   218	  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
   219	    (NatIso.ofComponents
   220	      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)
   221	      (fun {_ _} _ => by
   222	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   223	        apply LinearMap.ext
   224	        intro x
   225	        rfl))
   226

    10	/-!
    11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
    14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
    15	
    16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
    17	
    18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
    19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
    20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
    21	anywhere in the statement.
    22	
    23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
    24	
    25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
    26	
    27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
    28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
    29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
    30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
    31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
    32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
    33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
    34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
    35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
    36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
    37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
    38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
    39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
    40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
    41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
    42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
    43	
    44	## What this buys, stated exactly
    45	
    46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
    47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
    48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
    49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
    50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
    51	this tree.
    52	
    53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
    54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
    55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
    56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
    57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
    58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
    59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
    60	
    61	## What this does NOT do
    62	
    63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
    64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
    65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
    66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
    67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
    68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
    69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
    70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
    71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
    72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
    73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
    74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
    75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
    76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
    77	
    78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
    79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
    80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
    81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
    82	
    83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
    84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
    85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
    86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
    87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
    88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
    89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
    90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
    91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
    92	
    93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
    94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
    95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
    96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
    97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
    98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
    99	
   100	## Main declarations
   101	
   102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
   103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
   104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
   105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
   106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
   107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
   108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
   110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
   111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
   112	  arbitrary field.
   113	-/

   124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

   131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
   132	
   133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
   134	
   135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
   136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
   137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
   138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
   139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
   140	
   141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
   142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
   143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
   147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
   148	  rfl
   149	
   150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
   151	
   152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
   153	
   154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
   155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
   156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
   157	
   158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
   159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
   160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
   161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
   164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
   165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
   166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
   167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
   168	
   169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
   170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
   171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
   172	
   173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
   174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
   175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
   179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
   181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
   182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
   183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
   184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩

   188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
   189	
   190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
   191	class, at genus `0`.
   192	
   193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
   194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
   195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
   196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
   197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
   198	triviality at genus `0`.

   200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
   201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
   202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
   203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   220	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   222	  refine D.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero hg p ?_
   223	  rw [D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
   224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
   225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _

   227	/-! ## The engine, with no fibrewise hypothesis -/
   228	
   229	/-- **The rigid engine from a `pic⁰` membership**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite
   230	projective over `B`, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   231	
   232	No fibrewise clause appears in the statement: the hypotheses are the membership, its
   233	presentation, and the engine's own `IsNoetherianRing B`. -/
   234	theorem rigidEngine_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
   235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :
   239	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
   240	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
   241	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   242	  D.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h)
   243	
   244	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE, FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP** — the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1` at every
   245	prime of the test ring, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   246	
   247	This is the cohomological output the classical seesaw argument consumes next.  What it does not
   248	supply is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`; see the module docstring. -/
   249	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   250	    [IsNoetherianRing B] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   251	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   252	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   253	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   254	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   255	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   256	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h) p
   257

   260	/-! ## The presentation binder is FREE for classes from `relPic`
   261

name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`

a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.
